experience.reason: The reference to "Sol" breaks the immersive, second-person intimacy of the piece by introducing an external, meta-fictional author figure without sufficient context, causing the reader to step out of the narrative and into critical analysis.
The shift to visceral body horror ("ribs are my architecture") feels tonally disjointed from the preceding metaphysical grief, breaking the established thematic consistency without earning the pivot.

The abrupt introduction of the proper noun "Orachys" feels like an arbitrary lore dump that breaks the intimate, psychological tension established by the Voyd's voice, shifting from personal haunting to generic fantasy exposition without sufficient narrative grounding.

The sudden introduction of an unestablished character ("Orachys") breaks the intimate, direct address between the Voyd and the player, causing a jarring tonal shift that feels like lore-dumping rather than organic narrative progression.
